title: Construct Uniform Parity Array II
summary: Given an array nums1 of n distinct integers, determine if it is possible to construct another array nums2 of the same length such that all elements in nums2 are either all odd or all even.
statement: Given an array nums1 of n distinct integers, determine if it is possible to construct another array nums2 of the same length such that all elements in nums2 are either all odd or all even. For each index i, you can choose either nums2[i] = nums1[i] or nums2[i] = nums1[i] - nums1[j] for some j != i, with the condition that nums1[i] - nums1[j] must be at least 1. Return true if such an array can be constructed, otherwise return false.
constraints: At i, keep nums1[i] or replace it by a positive difference nums1[i]-nums1[j] for j≠i.
Return whether all resulting values can be made the same parity.
hints: An all-even result is automatic only when every original value is even; otherwise target odd parity.
Every odd value may stay unchanged. An even value can become positive odd exactly by subtracting a smaller odd value.
Find the smallest odd value and verify that every even value is larger than it.
That smallest odd supplies every needed conversion; if an even is smaller, no positive odd subtraction is available for that position.
editorial: That smallest odd supplies every needed conversion; if an even is smaller, no positive odd subtraction is available for that position.

tests.explanation: Keep the odd values and replace four by 4-1=3, producing all odd values.
Two can become one by subtracting one, so both positions can be odd.
